review-20260822-001.title: Limited comparison operators
review-20260822-001.body:
Only == and != operators are implemented. Other operators (>, >=, <, <=)
silently return false. This may be intentional for simplicity, but should
be documented or extended if needed.

review-20260822-002.title: Silent nil return when WatchService unavailable
review-20260822-002.body:
When the WatchService is not available, this function returns nil without an error.
This could make debugging difficult in production. Consider returning an error
or logging a warning when the WatchService is unavailable.

review-20260822-003.title: Silent nil return when WatchService unavailable
review-20260822-003.body:
When the WatchService is not available, this function returns nil without an error.
This could make debugging difficult in production. Consider returning an error
or logging a warning when the WatchService is unavailable.

review-20260822-004.title: Incorrect func pointer comparison in unsubscribe closure
review-20260822-004.body:
Fixed by using reflect.ValueOf to compare function pointers instead of
comparing addresses of loop variables. The original `&h == &handler`
compared the address of the loop variable `h` with the address of the
captured `handler` parameter, which would never match.

review-20260822-005.title: Document() returns mutable pointer after releasing lock
review-20260822-005.body:
This method acquires RLock, obtains a raw *document.Document pointer, releases
the lock via defer RUnlock, and returns the pointer. Callers can then mutate the
document freely without any lock held, creating a data race with concurrent
Read/Update/Transact calls. The mutex is effectively pointless for this method.

Fix by returning a defensive copy, returning an interface, or documenting that
the caller must not mutate the returned value.

review-20260822-006.title: Emit silently discards all handler errors
review-20260822-006.body:
Every handler error is discarded via `_ = h(ctx, evt)`. If a subscriber returns
an error indicating a failed write, dropped event, or context cancellation, the
caller has no way to know. This defeats Go's error propagation idiom.

go-events ScopedBus.Publish() returns errors. Migrating to ScopedBus would
fix this at the call site — callers can handle or propagate errors.
At minimum, log the error; ideally, collect errors from all handlers and return
them or pass them through a provided error channel.

review-20260822-007.title: Unreachable branch in CauseMessage
review-20260822-007.body:
Fixed by removing the dead `if se.Cause == nil` branch which was only
reachable when se.Message was empty, returning a useless empty string.

review-20260822-008.title: Clone acquires RLock then calls ExportJSON which also acquires RLock
review-20260822-008.body:
Clone() holds RLock and calls s.ExportJSON(), which itself acquires RLock.
While Go allows multiple concurrent readers, a pending writer between the two
lock acquisitions will cause deadlock. The RLock is not reentrant in the presence
of a writer — if ExportJSON is ever changed to use Lock, or if a writer is queued,
this deadlocks.

Fix by having Clone call an internal unexported exportJSONLocked method that
assumes the lock is already held.

review-20260822-010.title: Payload and Patch lack doc comments
review-20260822-010.body:
Fixed by adding doc comments explaining that Payload contains matched event
data and Patch contains state updates to apply on resume.

review-20260822-011.title: Untyped string for operator, field, and mode
review-20260822-011.body:
WatchCondition.Op, WatchCondition.Field, and WatchDescriptor.Mode are bare string
types with no compile-time validation. Invalid operator names like "eqq" or modes
like "ALL" will silently pass through. Define `type ConditionOp string` with
constants (OpEqual, OpNotEqual, etc.) and `type WatchMode string` to catch invalid
values at compile time.

review-20260822-012.title: Timeout is int64 without documented units
review-20260822-012.body:
WatchDescriptor.Timeout is int64 with no documentation of whether the value is in
milliseconds, seconds, or nanoseconds. Different callers will interpret this
differently. Change to time.Duration for type-safe, unambiguous units, or add a
clear doc comment specifying the unit.

review-20260822-013.title: WatchService has no error returns
review-20260822-013.body:
WatchService.Register returns nothing, so a registration failure (duplicate run ID,
invalid descriptor, resource exhaustion) is silently dropped. PeekBufferedEvent
returns *WatchEvent where nil means "no event," but this is ambiguous with a system
error. Register should return error, and PeekBufferedEvent should return
(WatchEvent, bool) or (WatchEvent, error).

review-20260822-016.title: Emit reads parent and underlying without lock protection
review-20260822-016.body:
Emit reads b.parent and b.underlying without holding any lock. While these fields
are only set during Scope() construction and are structurally immutable after that,
there is no enforcement or documentation of this immutability contract. A future
refactor adding post-construction mutation would silently introduce a data race.

Add a doc comment stating immutability, or protect with a lock.

review-20260822-017.title: Subscribe holds write lock for append-only operation
review-20260822-017.body:
Subscribe acquires b.mu.Lock() (exclusive write lock) but only appends to a slice.
For a read-heavy system where subscriptions are infrequent but Emit is called
constantly, a copy-on-write pattern with RLock for Emit and atomic slice
replacement for Subscribe would reduce contention. Not a correctness issue, but a
performance consideration at scale.

review-20260822-018.title: Document() returns concrete pointer, unmockable
review-20260822-018.body:
Store.Document() returns *document.Document, a concrete struct from the anansi
library. This makes it impossible to mock Store in tests without importing the
real document package. Consider returning an interface or removing Document() from
the Store interface entirely (callers can use Read() for safe access).

review-20260822-019.title: Transact is identical to Update
review-20260822-019.body:
Transact and Update have the same lock pattern, same signature shape, and same
semantics. Transact provides no rollback, retry, or isolation guarantees beyond
Update. This violates the Interface Segregation Principle and confuses callers about
which to use. Either add real transactional semantics (retry on conflict, nested
transactions, rollback) or remove Transact from the interface.

review-20260822-020.title: ExportJSON performs wasteful Marshal/Unmarshal round-trip
review-20260822-020.body:
ExportJSON marshals the document to []byte via json.Marshal, then immediately
unmarshals back into map[string]any. This is a redundant encode/decode cycle.

Either json.Unmarshal directly into map[string]any from the document's internal
representation, or add a ToMap() method to the document type.

review-20260822-021.title: Blank import side-effect is unexplained
review-20260822-021.body:
`var _ = data.DocumentIDField` is a blank variable assignment that asserts nothing
about types. Unlike `var _ Interface = (*Type)(nil)`, it has no compile-time
verification purpose. If it exists to force an import for side effects, it should use
`_ "package/path"` import syntax instead.

review-20260822-022.title: Variadic string for single message is awkward
review-20260822-022.body:
NewSystemError accepts variadic `message ...string` but callers must remember to
pass at most one message. Passing multiple strings produces an unpredictable joined
message or ignores extras. A single named `message string` parameter would be clearer
and catch misuse at compile time.

review-20260822-023.title: Cycle-detection logic undocumented
review-20260822-023.body:
CauseMessage includes a `seen` map for cycle detection but has no comment explaining
why cycles are possible in the error chain. Future maintainers may wonder why a
simple loop is insufficient.

review-20260822-024.title: UNAUTHORIZED conflated with PERMISSION_DENIED (401 vs 403)
review-20260822-024.body:
UNAUTHORIZED maps to httpStatus 403 and action "authorize". In HTTP semantics, 401
means "not authenticated" (no credentials) and 403 means "not authorized"
(insufficient permissions). These are distinct failure modes with different client
recovery strategies. Map UNAUTHORIZED to 401 and action "authenticate", or split
into separate cases.

review-20260822-025.title: HTTP status 499 is non-standard
review-20260822-025.body:
499 is an nginx invention for "client closed connection." It is not part of the HTTP
specification and will confuse clients, monitoring tools, and API documentation
generators. Use 499 only if you control the client, otherwise map ABORTED/CANCELLED
to 408 (Request Timeout) or 409 (Conflict), or document the custom status code
prominently.

review-20260822-026.title: INTERNAL_ERROR code not defined in errors.go constants
review-20260822-026.body:
The systemErrorMeta switch uses "INTERNAL_ERROR" as a case, but errors.go defines
ErrCodeExecutionFailed = "EXECUTION_FAILED", not "INTERNAL_ERROR". If a SystemError
is created with ErrCodeExecutionFailed, it falls to the default branch and maps to
system/500/internal anyway — but this is accidental, not intentional. The code
constants and the meta mapping are inconsistent.

review-20260822-027.title: Timestamp uses serialization time, not error creation time
review-20260822-027.body:
time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339) captures the time when SystemErrorJSON is
called, not when the error was originally created. For debugging, the error's
creation time is far more useful. If SystemError has a Timestamp field, use it;
otherwise the serialization time may differ from the actual error time by seconds
or minutes, making log correlation unreliable.

review-20260822-028.title: Stack field is always empty string
review-20260822-028.body:
The serialized JSON always includes `"stack": ""` as an empty string. This is dead
data that wastes wire bytes and confuses consumers who expect a stack trace. Either
populate it with a real stack (using runtime.Callers) or omit the key entirely when
empty.

review-20260822-029.title: Issues slice is untyped []any
review-20260822-029.body:
The issues variable is []any containing map[string]any elements with keys "code",
"message", "path", "index", "severity". There is no compile-time guarantee these
keys are correct or consistently spelled. A dedicated IssueJSON struct would provide
type safety and IDE autocomplete.

review-20260822-033.title: Write discards store update error
review-20260822-033.body:
The error from r.store.Update is discarded with `_ =`. If the store update fails
(e.g., validation error, key collision), the pipeline continues with stale state.
This defeats Go's error propagation idiom. At minimum, log the error; ideally,
propagate it or return it to the caller.

review-20260822-034.title: Unsafe type assertion without comma-ok
review-20260822-034.body:
Fixed by using comma-ok type assertion to prevent runtime panics
when instruction is not a PauseInstruction.

review-20260822-035.title: Discarded comma-ok on type assertion
review-20260822-035.body:
cfg, _ := interpolated.(map[string]any) discards the comma-ok error. If Interpolate
returns a non-map (e.g., a string), cfg is nil and passed to def.Run, which will
nil-dereference on cfg["anyKey"]. The `if cfg == nil` guard only protects against
literal nil, not wrong-type returns.

review-20260822-036.title: New HTTP client per request
review-20260822-036.body:
client := &http.Client{} creates a new HTTP client per request with no connection
pooling and a nil Transport (no TLS tuning, no timeouts on dial/TLS/etc.). Should
use a package-level or injected client.

review-20260822-037.title: Unbounded response body read
review-20260822-037.body:
io.ReadAll(resp.Body) reads unbounded response into memory. A malicious endpoint
returning a multi-GB body will OOM the process. Use io.LimitReader(resp.Body,
maxBytes).

review-20260822-038.title: Timer leak in select
review-20260822-038.body:
time.After(timeout) creates a timer that is not stopped if the select completes via
done or ctx.Done(). This leaks a timer until it fires. Use time.NewTimer with
explicit Stop().

review-20260822-039.title: TOCTOU race in dispatch between lock acquisitions
review-20260822-039.body:
dispatch calls rt.mu.Unlock() at line 531 then rt.mu.Lock() again at line 540.
Between these two critical sections, rt.paused and rt.index could be mutated by
other goroutines (e.g., Deregister). The snapshot of toResume and entries is taken
under separate locks, creating a TOCTOU window.

Fix by taking both snapshots under a single lock acquisition, or by using a
snapshot that is immutable after release.

review-20260822-040.title: Discarded Schedule error
review-20260822-040.body:
The error from rt.scheduler.Schedule is silently discarded. If scheduling fails
(e.g., invalid cron expression), the trigger will never fire and the failure
will be invisible to the caller.

review-20260822-041.title: Goroutine leak when HTTP client disconnects
review-20260822-041.body:
handlePostRun spawns a goroutine that calls s.rt.Run(). If the HTTP client
disconnects (line 212 time.After), the goroutine continues running the workflow.
There is no cancellation of the ctx passed to rt.Run. The select on prep channel
has no default, and the goroutine may block sending to prep if the handler returns
early. The goroutine does check select with default on the error path, but the
success path (prep <- prepResult{runID: h.RunID}) blocks until consumed — if the
handler timed out, the goroutine blocks forever.

review-20260822-042.title: Timer leak in handlePostRun
review-20260822-042.body:
time.After(10 * time.Second) leaks a timer if the prep channel receives first. Use
time.NewTimer with defer timer.Stop().

review-20260822-043.title: Get returns mutable internal state pointer
review-20260822-043.body:
Get returns a pointer to the internal ActiveRun under RLock. After RUnlock, the
caller holds a reference to mutable internal state. If Deregister or MarkPaused is
called concurrently, the caller's ActiveRun may be modified or its timer stopped.

Fix by returning a copy of ActiveRun, or by documenting that the caller must not
mutate the returned value.

review-20260822-044.title: Unknown operator returns true
review-20260822-044.body:
The switch statement has no default case. Unknown operators (e.g., ">", "<=")
silently fall through and return true (the loop continues). This means invalid
conditions are treated as satisfied, which could cause incorrect event matching.
Add a default case that returns false for unrecognized operators.

review-20260822-045.title: Double registration of pause node
review-20260822-045.body:
nodes.go registers pause.Node on line 31, and pause.go also registers itself in its
own init() on line 125. Since Register overwrites by kind, this is a harmless race
but signals confusion about ownership. Remove the init() in pause.go.

review-20260822-046.title: Store update errors silently discarded
review-20260822-046.body:
_ = nCtx.Store.Update(ctx, store.SetValue(k, v)) discards the store update
error. If the patch fails, the router still jumps to onResume with stale
state. At minimum, log the error; ideally, propagate it.

review-20260822-048.title: Store update errors discarded when folding resume payload
review-20260822-048.body:
_ = st.Update(...) discards the error when folding the resume event payload
into state. If the store rejects the update, the resumed pipeline will run
with incomplete state.

review-20260822-050.title: Wildcard CORS origin
review-20260822-050.body:
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * allows any origin to access the API. In production,
restrict to specific trusted origins. This is a security risk if the API is
exposed to the internet.

review-20260822-051.title: JSON encoder error discarded
review-20260822-051.body:
json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(data) error is discarded. If encoding fails after
WriteHeader, the client gets a partial/corrupt response. At minimum, log the error.

review-20260822-052.title: Context never propagated to callback
review-20260822-052.body:
context.WithCancel(context.Background()) creates a context that is never propagated
to the callback. The cancel is called in Cancel() and Shutdown(), but the callback
at line 56 receives context.Background(), not the cancellable context. The context
is unused — either pass it to the callback or remove it.

review-20260822-053.title: CronDelay silently masks invalid cron expressions
review-20260822-053.body:
CronDelay returns time.Hour as a fallback when @every parse fails. This
silently masks invalid cron expressions. Consider logging the error or
returning a sentinel.

review-20260822-054.title: Marshal/Unmarshal round-trip in WriteCheckpoint
review-20260822-054.body:
WriteCheckpoint marshals ckpt to JSON, then immediately unmarshals it back into
map[string]any. This is a pointless double-serialization to satisfy
SetMetadataValue. If SetMetadataValue truly needs a raw map, marshal the struct
directly to the target map using a single pass, or change the API.

review-20260822-055.title: Goroutine leak on normal path
review-20260822-055.body:
A goroutine is spawned per Run call to bridge abortChan -> cancel(). On the normal
(non-aborted) path, this goroutine blocks on select until runCtx.Done() fires. The
defer cancel() ensures the context is cancelled, so the goroutine will eventually
drain — but there is a brief window where the goroutine outlives the Run return. If
Run is called in a tight loop, these goroutines accumulate transiently. Consider
using context.AfterFunc (Go 1.21+) instead of a dedicated goroutine.

review-20260825-001.title: Discarded store update error in result merge
review-20260825-001.body:
The error from r.store.Update is discarded with `_ =`. If the store
update fails (e.g., document corruption, write conflict), the parent
silently loses the child's result with no indication. At minimum,
log the error; ideally, return it or fail the stage.

review-20260825-002.title: Shared initialState across concurrent goroutines
review-20260825-002.body:
The initialState map is extracted once and shared across all child goroutines
that call NewFreshStore(initialState). If any child mutates the map (e.g., via
a code node), other children see the mutation. This is unlikely since
NewFreshStore copies the map into a document, but the map itself is not
deep-copied before being passed. Consider deep-copying initialState per
child if mutation is possible.

review-20260825-003.title: Error string ends with period
review-20260825-003.body:
Go convention: error strings should not end with punctuation.
Change to: fmt.Errorf("pipeline-ref node %s has no pipelineId configured", id)

review-20260825-004.title: Error string ends with period
review-20260825-004.body: Go convention: error strings should not end with punctuation.

review-20260825-005.title: Wasteful JSON round-trip for result merging
review-20260825-005.body:
json.Marshal then json.Unmarshal is a wasteful encode/decode cycle.
Consider adding a ToMap() method to document.Document, or use
sRes.FinalDoc.Data() directly if it returns the underlying map.

scoped-bus-opportunity-001.title: Replace MemoryScopedBus with go-events ScopedBus for topic isolation
scoped-bus-opportunity-001.body:
The go-events/v2 package now provides ScopedBus (scoped.go) which gives
real topic-level namespace isolation via topic prefixing. MemoryScopedBus
uses hierarchical bubbling but no actual topic isolation — all scopes
share the same flat event type namespace.

go-events ScopedBus benefits for hermes:
  - bus.Scope("run:"+runID) gives per-run topic isolation (no cross-run interference)
  - bus.Scope("workflow:"+wfID) gives per-workflow isolation
  - IsolatedScope() creates a separate Pebble store for true data isolation
  - Publish() returns errors (current Emit discards all handler errors — P1 review note)
  - Durable event log via Pebble (the underlying field is currently never wired)

Migration path:
  1. Replace NewMemoryScopedBus() with NewEventBus() + ScopedBus usage
  2. Replace Emit() calls with scoped.Publish() (error-returning)
  3. Remove manual parent-bubbling logic (ScopedBus handles it internally)
  4. Wire the durable backend that was designed but never connected

scoped-bus-opportunity-002.title: Orphan bus fallback silently loses all events
scoped-bus-opportunity-002.body:
When no bus is provided and factory has no EventBus option, a standalone
MemoryScopedBus is created with no parent and no underlying go-events bus.
Events emitted on this bus go nowhere — no subscribers, no bubbling, no
timeline recording. This is a silent data loss scenario.

Fix with go-events ScopedBus: use bus.IsolatedScope(runID) from the root
runtime bus instead of creating orphan buses. This ensures every pipeline
execution has a durable event log and proper scoping.

scoped-bus-opportunity-003.title: Empty EventPath scoping provides no real isolation
scoped-bus-opportunity-003.body:
Per-run buses are scoped with an empty EventPath{}. The path is only used
for metadata decoration (populated into PipelineEvent.Path for the frontend
timeline) — it does NOT filter or route events. All runs share the same
flat namespace on the root bus.

Fix with go-events ScopedBus: use bus.Scope("run:"+runID) instead of
bus.Scope(EventPath{}). This gives actual topic isolation — each run's
events are prefixed with its runID, preventing cross-run interference.

scoped-bus-opportunity-004.title: WatchService subscribes to root bus and manually filters by runID
scoped-bus-opportunity-004.body:
The WatchService subscribes to the root runtime bus for all watched event
types. When a watched event arrives, it fans out to ALL runs waiting for
that event type via the byEventType reverse index, then each run's onEvent
handler manually checks if the event belongs to it.

With go-events ScopedBus, the WatchService could subscribe to per-run
scoped buses (bus.Scope("run:"+runID)) instead of the root bus. This
eliminates manual runID filtering and reduces unnecessary fan-out.

scoped-bus-opportunity-005.title: Durable event backend designed but never wired
scoped-bus-opportunity-005.body:
NewMemoryScopedBus accepts an optional go-events SimpleEventBus for
durable Pebble LSM event sourcing (designed in the spec). However,
the runtime never passes one — the underlying field is always nil.
All events are purely in-memory and lost on restart.

Fix with go-events ScopedBus: create a root EventBus with Pebble-backed
Config, then use bus.Scope() for per-run and per-workflow isolation.
This gives durable event logs, checkpoint recovery, and compaction
out of the box.
